funder_type_other_description: Dutch charitable foundation (stichting), not a US 501(c)(3) entity
stated_mission: Supporting the open internet since 1997; funds open hardware, software, standards, science, and data that further an open internet commons.
funding_priorities: Core internet infrastructure (routing, DNS, encryption, decentralization)
Decentralized platforms with end-to-end encryption (ELFA fund)
grant_size_range: First proposal: max EUR 50,000 (0-50 kEuro). A proposal larger than EUR 50,000 must be preceded by one or more smaller NLnet-funded projects that have been successfully concluded first.
typical_grant_period: Unclear -- milestone/deliverable-based disbursement is typical of NGI-style programs, not confirmed for current funds
application_cycle: Calls currently closed ('not possible to submit proposals' as of 2026-08-20); new calls across several funds reopen 2026-09-03 with a 2026-11-03 12:00 CEST deadline. NLnet is transitioning from its NGI Zero program (including the User-Operated Internet Fund) to a new 'Open Internet Stack' effort and other programmes -- which named funds (Restack/CodeSupply/ELFA/other) will be open in the September cycle is not yet confirmed.
application_process: Apply directly via nlnet.nl/propose/ following the fund-specific guide; proposals must be submitted in English
eligibility_requirements: CONFIRMED directly on nlnet.nl/useroperated/eligibility/ (User-Operated Internet Fund page): 'There are no categorical exclusions of persons or entities who may not receive support from this fund. There are no geographical restrictions.' No legal entity or fiscal sponsor is required -- individuals and informal/not-yet-established organizations can apply directly.
Must release software/hardware/content under libre/open licenses and apply open standards where possible -- a hard requirement across all funds.

This specific confirmation was read on the User-Operated Internet Fund's guide, which is under NGI Zero -- a program NLnet is currently sunsetting in favor of a new 'Open Internet Stack' effort. Whether the same no-entity-required policy explicitly carries over to the new funds (Restack, CodeSupply, ELFA) that reopen 2026-09-03 is very likely but not yet directly confirmed against those specific fund pages.

Fund scope leans toward core internet/protocol-level infrastructure and general FOSS software engineering/security/documentation/usability work (per the UOI fund's list of qualifying activities) -- GASify/geoCRM's dependency on the proprietary Google Apps Script platform remains a real tension with this scope; build-tools/typescript-build-config (platform-agnostic dev tooling) is more likely to fit than geoCRM itself.

mission_alignment.doikayt_overlap: build-tools and typescript-build-config are generic, platform-agnostic open-source developer tooling and could plausibly fit a supply-chain/infrastructure framing (e.g. CodeSupply). GASify and geoCRM are built specifically on Google Apps Script/Workspace, which is in real tension with NLnet's open-standards/open-internet ethos -- that is Doikayt building on top of Big Tech infrastructure, not away from it, at the technical layer, even though Doikayt's broader mission (grassroots orgs controlling their own tools) points the other direction.
potential_concerns: GASify/geoCRM's dependency on proprietary Google Apps Script is a real tension against NLnet's open-standards/open-internet mission, not just an open question

Deadline 2026-11-03, cycle reopens 2026-09-03 -- enough lead time to research properly before rushing an application
mission_alignment.best_fit_framing: Untested. org_name: Sovereign Tech Fund / Sovereign Tech Agency
stated_mission: A German government-backed agency (Sovereign Tech Agency) that funds and strengthens critical open source infrastructure the digital ecosystem depends on, for security, resilience, and technological diversity.
funding_priorities: Security and maintenance of foundational software dependencies
grant_size_range: Minimum roughly EUR 50,000 (cost of proposed work must exceed this); no fixed upper limit
application_cycle: Unclear/rolling (one third-party project-fundraising tracker lists it as 'Rolling Deadline')
application_process: Apply via sovereign.tech/programs/fund; a separate Fellowship program exists with its own freelance (global) and employment (Germany-only) tracks
eligibility_requirements: CONFIRMED on sovereign.tech/programs/fund: 'We do not finance the development of prototypes' and 'we are currently not looking for user-facing applications, such as messaging apps or file storage services.' This clearly excludes geoCRM (a user-facing CRM app, currently prototype-stage). It does NOT clearly exclude GASify itself -- GASify is a developer framework/tooling layer, not a user-facing application, and is closer to STF's stated target category ('administration tools for developers,' 'libraries for programming languages').
CONFIRMED: cost of proposed work must exceed EUR 50,000 (current minimum) -- a real stretch to scope credibly at Doikayt's current stage regardless of which project is pitched.

CONFIRMED 'Prevalence' criterion: funded technology must already be widely used/relied upon, with notable projects or organizations depending on it. This is the binding blocker for GASify specifically -- it has no confirmed external adopters yet, independent of the user-facing-application question.
Whether GASify itself counts as still-'prototype' in STF's sense, as opposed to geoCRM specifically, is unconfirmed.
CONFIRMED: not eligible if another public entity is already funding the same proposed activities.
Code/documentation must be freely reusable under OSI/FSF-approved licenses with no non-commercial or no-derivative clauses.

mission_alignment.sponsor_mission_summary: German government-backed agency funding maintenance and resilience of critical, widely-used open source infrastructure that societies and economies already depend on.
mission_alignment.doikayt_overlap: GASify (the framework layer, not geoCRM) is conceptually closer to STF's target category than initially assessed -- it's developer tooling/infrastructure, not a user-facing application, so the 'not looking for user-facing applications' exclusion doesn't clearly apply to it. The binding blocker is Prevalence: GASify has no confirmed external adopters yet, and STF explicitly funds technology already widely relied upon, not new frameworks seeking their first users.
potential_concerns: Prevalence bar: GASify isn't yet widely used/relied upon by others -- this is the real blocker, not the user-facing-application criterion
Whether GASify itself (vs geoCRM) would be read as still-prototype-stage by STF is unconfirmed
Government-of-Germany funded -- worth confirming no geographic/citizenship restriction applies in practice
mission_alignment.best_fit_framing: Revisit once GASify (not geoCRM) has meaningful external adoption -- other developers or projects actually building on the framework, not just Doikayt's own use of it. At that point GASify's framing as developer infrastructure, not a user-facing app, becomes a real asset rather than a moot distinction.
